title: Basic data types
content:
# Basic data types Computer data comes in many forms: text, images, video, audio, 3D models, and more. Although organized differently, all these forms are built from basic data types. **Basic data types are types on which the CPU can operate directly** and which algorithms use directly. The main types include the following. - Integer types: `byte`, `short`, `int`, and `long`. - Floating-point types: `float` and `double`, used to represent fractional numbers. - The character type `char`, used for letters in different languages, punctuation, and even emoji. - The Boolean type `bool`, used for yes-or-no values. **Basic data types are stored in binary form**. One binary digit is $1$ bit. In the vast majority of modern operating systems, $1$ byte consists of $8$ bits. A basic data type's value range depends on the space it occupies. Taking Java as an example: - An integer `byte` occupies $1$ byte = $8$ bits and can represent $2^{8}$ distinct values. - An integer `int` occupies $4$ bytes = $32$ bits and can represent $2^{32}$ distinct values. The table below lists storage sizes, value ranges, and default values for Java's basic data types. There is no need to memorize it; understand the general picture and refer back when needed.

Table   Storage sizes and value ranges of basic data types

| Type | Name | Storage size | Minimum value | Maximum value | Default value | | ------ | -------- | -------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------- | -------------- | | Integer | `byte` | 1 byte | $-2^7$ ($-128$) | $2^7 - 1$ ($127$) | $0$ | | | `short` | 2 bytes | $-2^{15}$ | $2^{15} - 1$ | $0$ | | | `int` | 4 bytes | $-2^{31}$ | $2^{31} - 1$ | $0$ | | | `long` | 8 bytes | $-2^{63}$ | $2^{63} - 1$ | $0$ | | Floating-point | `float` | 4 bytes | $1.175 \times 10^{-38}$ | $3.403 \times 10^{38}$ | $0.0\text{f}$ | | | `double` | 8 bytes | $2.225 \times 10^{-308}$ | $1.798 \times 10^{308}$ | $0.0$ | | Character | `char` | 2 bytes | $0$ | $2^{16} - 1$ | $0$ | | Boolean | `bool` | 1 byte | $\text{false}$ | $\text{true}$ | $\text{false}$ | The table above describes Java's basic data types. Each programming language defines its own types, whose sizes, value ranges, and default values may differ. - In Python, an `int` can be arbitrarily large, limited only by available memory. A `float` is a 64-bit double-precision number. There is no `char` type: a single character is a `str` of length 1. - C and C++ do not fix the sizes of basic data types; they vary by implementation and platform. The table above follows the LP64 [data model](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/types#Properties), used by 64-bit Unix operating systems including Linux and macOS. - A `char` occupies 1 byte in C and C++. In most programming languages, character size depends on the encoding used; see the character encoding section. - Although a Boolean needs only 1 bit ($0$ or $1$), it usually occupies 1 byte in memory because modern CPUs typically use a byte as the smallest addressable memory unit. How do basic data types relate to data structures? A data structure is a way to organize and store data in a computer. The emphasis is on structure, rather than the data itself. To represent a row of numbers, an array comes naturally to mind. Its linear structure captures adjacency and ordering, regardless of whether the stored values are integers (`int`), fractional numbers (`float`), or characters (`char`). In other words, **basic data types specify what kind of data is stored, while data structures specify how it is organized**.
